Class JumpReset

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.JumpReset
public final class JumpReset extends Object
The way out of a combo that gives the opponent no room: on the tick it learns of a hit of a combo it is taking (the second in a row or a later one), with its feet still on the ground, which they are for that one tick, it jumps with W and the sprint key held. A running jump adds a fifth of a block a tick towards where it is looking, against a knockback of four tenths (seven with a sprint behind the hit): it is thrown half as far, or two thirds. It comes down within a sword's reach of the opponent instead of beyond it, and the swing it owes (AnswerRule) is there to be made. What players call a jump reset.

Why it is needed. Up to the first evening of 0.14.0 against people, the way out of a combo was S alone (BackNudge): back off, and come in again for the first hit. Against a player who answers that with a running jump it is the way into the next hit. A running jump covers ground faster than S does, the one who comes in sees the one who backs off where it was a moment ago, which is nearer, and the hit at the end of the jump is a critical one; that throws the fighter back again, S again, and so on round. Backing off is what that player's combo is made of.

Only ever in a combo, never on the first hit: a fighter that takes no hit at its full knockback cannot be comboed at all, by anyone, and that is not a fight. And only this share of those hits (Config.jumpResetChance).

And a hit that finds it with its sword on the way back from a hit of its own (counters): the opponent's answer to that hit, made before there is a swing to answer it with. Jumped with, the fighter is thrown half as far and is in the air beside the opponent as its sword comes back, and the swing it owes is made on the way down, a critical hit. Without that, an opponent that follows its answer with a running jump has the fighter twice for each hit the fighter lands.

With one exception more (chasers): an opponent that has followed a hit with a second one made from the air, which is the running jump and the critical hit, is one that does. Against that opponent, for the next twenty seconds, the first hit is jumped with as well. Its second hit is on its way the moment the first has landed, and a fighter that has jumped with the first is coming down on it, sword back, while it is still going up.

Not thread-safe; one per fighter.

    • plan

      public int plan(float[] vec, int keys, boolean hitNow)
      One decision.
      Parameters:
      vec - what the network is shown on this tick
      keys - the keys that are the network's on this tick
      hitNow - the body's own game has learned of a hit on it since the last decision: it has the knockback and its feet are still on the ground. On a server that is the tick the player is seen to flinch.
      Returns:
      what this tick is to do, as JumpIn's flags; 0 leaves everything to the network and to the other rules
